title: SQL Server queries timing out under load on OrdersDB
description: Application reported request timeouts and SqlException: Timeout expired errors during peak hours. Multiple sessions were queued waiting on the same table.
root_cause: A long-running reporting query was holding row locks on the Orders table, blocking OLTP writes from the order-service. The blocking session (spid) had been open for over 20 minutes.
resolution: Killed the blocking SQL session, added a NOLOCK-safe reporting replica, and scheduled the report to run off-peak.
next_step: Run sys.dm_exec_requests filtered by blocking_session_id to identify the head blocker, then check its wait_type and last executed query text.

title: Kafka consumer group lag growing unbounded on billing-events topic
description: Consumer lag alert fired for the billing-events-consumer-group on topic billing.events.v1. Downstream billing records were delayed by over an hour.
root_cause: One consumer instance in the group was stuck in a retry loop calling a downstream API that was returning 429 Too Many Requests, blocking partition processing for the whole group.
resolution: Restarted the stuck consumer instance, added exponential backoff with a circuit breaker on the downstream call, and added a per-partition lag alert.
next_step: Check consumer group lag per partition (kafka-consumer-groups --describe) and inspect the stuck consumer's thread dump for the partition it owns.

title: IIS 502.3 Bad Gateway on checkout-api after deployment
description: Users hit intermittent 502.3 Bad Gateway errors on the checkout API. Windows Event Viewer showed the w3wp.exe worker process for the app pool terminating unexpectedly.
root_cause: An unhandled NullReferenceException in a new pricing-calculation code path crashed the IIS worker process (w3wp.exe), which IIS then restarted mid-request, producing 502.3 for in-flight requests.
resolution: Rolled back the deployment, added null checks around the pricing calculation, and added an IIS Application Pool rapid-fail-protection alert.
next_step: Check Windows Event Viewer Application log for w3wp.exe crash events and the IIS Application Pool recycling/failure history around the timestamps of the 502 errors.

title: Meter communication timeout for a batch of endpoints on collector COLL-14
description: A batch of ~40 meters stopped reporting interval data. Collector COLL-14 logs showed repeated CommandTimeout errors when polling the affected meter endpoints.
root_cause: A firmware update pushed to the mesh network router serving those endpoints caused it to drop RF communication with the collector, so commands never reached the meters.
resolution: Rolled back the router firmware and re-triggered a full mesh network rebuild for the affected endpoint IDs.
next_step: Check the collector's command log for the affected meter/endpoint IDs to confirm whether commands are timing out at the RF/mesh layer versus the head-end system.

title: Kubernetes pod CrashLoopBackOff for payment-service
description: The payment-service deployment showed multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Pod events showed OOMKilled as the termination reason.
root_cause: A memory leak introduced in a recent release caused heap usage to grow until the container exceeded its memory limit and was OOMKilled by the kubelet.
resolution: Rolled back to the previous image, raised the memory limit temporarily, and opened a follow-up to fix the leak (unbounded in-memory cache).
next_step: Run kubectl describe pod on the affected pod to confirm OOMKilled, then check kubectl logs --previous for the last log lines before the container was killed.

title: RabbitMQ queue backlog on notifications.email queue
description: The notifications.email queue depth grew to over 500,000 messages with no consumers acknowledging messages.
root_cause: The consumer service lost its RabbitMQ connection after a network blip and did not automatically reconnect due to a missing connection-recovery configuration.
resolution: Restarted the consumer service, enabled automatic connection recovery in the RabbitMQ client, and added a queue-depth alert.
next_step: Check the RabbitMQ management UI for consumer count on the queue and check the consumer service logs for connection reset/channel error entries.

title: NullPointerException in order-service during checkout
description: Java stack traces showed java.lang.NullPointerException in OrderProcessor.calculateTotal when customers with an empty saved-address list attempted checkout.
root_cause: A recent refactor removed a null check on the customer's default shipping address, which is null for customers who never saved an address.
resolution: Added the null check back and a unit test covering customers with no saved address; deployed hotfix.
next_step: Search application logs for the exact exception type and stack trace frame (OrderProcessor.calculateTotal) across all order-service instances to gauge blast radius.

title: Intermittent 500 errors on /api/v1/orders due to downstream timeout
description: The orders API endpoint intermittently returned 500 errors. Correlation IDs showed the requests were spending most of their time waiting on the inventory-service call.
root_cause: The inventory-service was under-provisioned and its P99 latency exceeded the orders API's HTTP client timeout, causing the orders API to fail the whole request.
resolution: Scaled out inventory-service, increased the client timeout with a sane upper bound, and added a fallback for stale-but-available inventory data.
next_step: Trace the correlation ID across services to identify which downstream call is consuming most of the request latency before assuming the failure originates in the orders API itself.
